text: What is the Ring Drone Cam? Amazon's indoor flying camera, $250. The Ring Drone Cam is an indoor security drone made by Ring, the home security company owned by Amazon. Ring unveiled it on a Tuesday in a New York demonstration, priced at $250, and it flies from room to room to check on alarms and sensors in a home.. Amazon's Ring announced the Ring Drone Cam, an indoor flying camera, and asked whether people would let a drone fly inside their homes for security. The news comes amid renewed scrutiny of Ring's privacy practices.. The drone is about the size of a textbook. When a door, window or other Ring sensor is triggered, it follows a set path to look into the disturbance. Users can also send it out at any time. It can fly up to eight minutes before returning on its own to a charging dock. Its built-in LED lights, which Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff called a crime deterrent, are meant to be seen from outside, so an intruder may see lights moving past a window. Ring first previewed the drone in 2020 under the name Always Home Cam. Siminoff said the company delayed release until Amazon could improve the design, sensors and data processing. The same day, Ring also launched the $1,000 Ring Rover Cam, a wheeled robot built on Amazon's Astro home robot for businesses. Ring says the drone cannot fly outside, because Federal Aviation Administration rules require a pilot's line of sight, and that privacy is the default setting on both devices, with an LED light showing when recording. Why it matters now: the launch comes as Ring faces continued privacy questions, mainly over its work with police, and after it canceled a link with the police technology provider Flock Safety. Ring is owned by Amazon and is known for its doorbells, and the company says the drone expands its home monitoring range.

What is a Ring Rover Cam? Amazon's $999 indoor patrol robot. The Ring Rover Cam is a wheeled indoor security robot from Amazon's Ring unit, built to patrol businesses such as offices and warehouses. It carries a camera on a raised periscope arm, a siren, and a red light, and it costs $1,000 (listed at $999 for preorder).. Amazon's Ring unveiled the Rover Cam alongside an indoor flying drone, raising the question of whether people want a drone flying inside their homes for security.. The device is based on Amazon's Astro home robot, which the company introduced in 2021. Like Astro, it rolls on two large wheels and has a display on top, but it has no access to the Alexa voice assistant. Its screen shows status messages, including when it is recording, instead of animated eyes. Its 4K periscope camera can rise and lower to see over counters and shelves, and a stubby tower on top holds a siren, a flashing red light, and a blue light that is projected onto the ceiling so staff can find the robot in large rooms. A guard can send the robot to a chosen room, or it can follow a pre-programmed patrol route. It also moves on its own to any spot where another Ring alarm has been triggered. While traveling, it streams and records video, and on arrival it makes a 360-degree scan. Battery life is estimated at about 30 minutes, enough for a single floor of roughly 5,000 square feet. For buildings with several floors, the company suggests multiple robots or pairing it with the new Ring Drone Cam, a $250 flying unit for indoor use. Amazon made the announcement on a Tuesday at a demo in New York, where Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff presented the drone and the robot. The Rover Cam is the second attempt to turn Astro into a business security robot; in 2023 Amazon launched the $2,349.99 Astro for Business and discontinued it a year later. The same question of indoor surveillance is now drawing attention, since Ring has faced privacy concerns tied to its police partnerships. Ring says privacy is the default setting for both devices, and both flash an LED light when recording.

What is a hip pointer injury? Football's painful hip bruise. A hip pointer is a bruise, or contusion, on the upper outer part of the hip, caused by a direct blow to the iliac crest, the top ridge of the pelvis. It is common in contact sports such as football. Recovery usually takes one to three weeks, according to Norton Healthcare. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy has one.. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy is expected to play Nov. 12, 2026, despite a hip pointer suffered against the Eagles.. Norton Healthcare says hip pointers often happen in contact sports but can also come from a fall. Symptoms include bruising, swelling and tenderness of the hip, limited range of motion and pain that can be severe and usually gets worse with activity. Doctors advise getting checked to rule out a more serious injury. Standard care is rest, ice and compression as soon as possible; anti-inflammatory or pain medication may help, and gentle stretching can ease stiffness. If pain lasts more than a couple of weeks, Norton recommends seeing a doctor again. Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the former Minnesota Vikings starter, hurt his hip in the Giants' win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported it was a hip pointer. Coach John Harbaugh said Monday that McCarthy was "doing well" and expected to play Thursday, Nov. 12, against the Washington Commanders.

What is Win the Mall on Netflix? The shopping competition, explained. Win the Mall is a Netflix reality competition premiering Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Ten teams of expert shoppers compete inside a real, working shopping mall to take control of storefronts, grow their spending power and outmaneuver rivals. Content creator Haley Baylee hosts, and Fremantle produces the series.. Netflix's new shopping competition Win the Mall premieres Nov. 18, 2026, just ahead of the Black Friday shopping season.. Netflix calls the show "the ultimate fantasy retail experience" that turns "a classic American shopping mall into a thrilling game of strategy and unexpected twists." The official logline describes it as "part shopping spree, part social strategy." Only one contestant is crowned the winner and walks away with what the producers call "the keys to the ultimate prize"; Netflix has not said what the prize is or which mall was used. Special guests Jonathan Van Ness, Keith Lee, Salish Matter and Lilly Singh join Baylee for mall-themed challenges. Baylee, whose name is sometimes misspelled "Haylee Baylee," is a former scientist who became a full-time creator, host and model; she won Sports Illustrated's Model Search in 2017. Netflix announced the series on March 17, 2026. Jimmy Fox executive produces for Fremantle, with Charles Wachter as showrunner.

What is CME FedWatch? A tool that tracks Fed rate cut and hike odds. CME FedWatch is a free tool run by the CME Group, a Chicago-based exchange operator, that shows the odds traders assign to changes in the Federal Reserve's benchmark interest rate. It turns prices from federal funds futures contracts into percentage probabilities for each upcoming Fed meeting. The tool is also written as CME Fed Watch.. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than the 0.3% economists expected. Market odds for the Fed's December decision moved after the release.. The tool breaks those odds down by meeting date and by the size of a move, such as no change, a quarter-point hike, or a half-point hike. Traders and reporters use it as a snapshot of market expectations, not as a forecast from the Fed itself. The next Fed meeting covered in current coverage is set for Dec. 8-9. On the day of the October consumer price report, the tool showed traders had fully priced in a quarter-point increase at that meeting, while the odds of a half-point increase stood at 13.6%. The Fed's benchmark rate was held in a range of 3.75% to 4% at its October meeting, when officials voted 10-2 to keep it there. The tool gained attention after the Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% that economists had expected. Stock futures slipped and Treasury yields rose after the release, a sign that markets moved toward expecting higher rates for longer. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said on Oct. 28 that the central bank wants price increases to ease.

What is the Anthropic IPO? Date, price range and valuation. The Anthropic IPO is the planned first public sale of shares in Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot. Anthropic will list on the Nasdaq in New York this month, November 2026, at $70 to $78 per share, valuing the company at about $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion.. Anthropic has set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its stock market listing, valuing the company at up to about $1.3 trillion. The listing comes days after the US midterm elections, when AI-related stocks fell sharply.. Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion through the offering, according to the company's filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The shares will trade under the ticker symbol "ANT." Earlier, some analysts had predicted a valuation near $2 trillion, so the announced range is lower than those estimates. The timing is sensitive. After the US midterm elections last week, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns that a Democrat-led Congress could slow AI development and the building of data centers. Global stocks also dropped as those fears spread to Asia and Europe. Anthropic's revenue rose to $16.2 billion in the first six months of 2026 from $1.1 billion a year earlier. Its valuation in a May 2026 funding round was $965 billion. Anthropic is based in San Francisco and was founded in January 2021 by former OpenAI members, led by Dario Amodei as chief executive and Daniela Amodei as president. The company's filing says it expects to list in November 2026.
